note: tmgmt_google provides one TMGMT translator plugin, 'google' (GoogleTranslator), configured via a tmgmt_translator config entity (config tmgmt.translator.<id>) with plugin: google and settings api_key (required), auto_accept, url (hidden test override). It calls Google Translate API v2 (https://www.googleapis.com/language/translate/v2) in chunks of 5. This site has NO Google API key, so all medium/hard cases are grounded in the translator/provider PLUGIN CONFIG (the tmgmt_translator entity and its settings) and never trigger a live translation. Scripts create/read/delete a tmgmt_translator entity; cleanup/reset remove it to restore baseline. The site already has an unrelated translator 'tmgmtg_cfg' (plugin google_v3) which the scripts do not touch.

evals.prompt: The Drupal module tmgmt_google adds a machine translator to TMGMT. What is the translator plugin id it registers, and which setting holds the Google credential it needs?
evals.expected_output: It registers the TMGMT translator plugin id 'google' (GoogleTranslator). The credential is stored in the translator's api_key setting (the Google Cloud Translation API key).

evals.prompt: In tmgmt_google, what must be configured before the Google translator reports itself as available for TMGMT jobs, and how is that value checked when saving the provider?
evals.expected_output: An api_key (Google API key) must be set: checkAvailable() returns yes only when api_key is present. On saving the provider the UI validates the key by fetching Google's supported languages and errors if none come back.

evals.prompt: Which Google service/endpoint does tmgmt_google use to translate TMGMT job data, and how does it batch the source strings?
evals.expected_output: It calls Google Translate API v2 at https://www.googleapis.com/language/translate/v2, sending source strings in chunks of 5 (qChunkSize) with source/target/q parameters.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a TMGMT translator (provider) named tmgg_eval. Inspect the live configuration and report which translator plugin it uses.
evals.expected_output: It uses the 'google' plugin: the tmgmt_translator entity tmgg_eval (config tmgmt.translator.tmgg_eval) has plugin: google.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the TMGMT Google translator named tmgg_auto_eval has been configured. Inspect its live settings and report whether it automatically accepts translations (the auto_accept setting).
evals.expected_output: Yes, it auto-accepts: tmgmt.translator.tmgg_auto_eval has settings.auto_accept = true.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, add a TMGMT translation provider that uses the Google Translator (plugin 'google'), with machine name tmgg_task, and set its Google API key to 'EVAL-KEY-123'. Apply the change to the live site. (Do not attempt a live translation.)
evals.expected_output: A tmgmt_translator entity tmgg_task exists with plugin 'google' and settings.api_key = 'EVAL-KEY-123' (e.g. Translator::create(['name'=>'tmgg_task','plugin'=>'google','settings'=>['api_key'=>'EVAL-KEY-123']]) or the Add provider UI).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a TMGMT Google translator with machine name tmgg_autotask (plugin 'google'). Configure it to automatically accept translations, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: tmgmt.translator.tmgg_autotask has settings.auto_accept = true (set the auto_accept setting on the tmgmt_translator entity).
